skill.name: error-detective
skill.description: Search logs and codebases for error patterns, stack traces, and anomalies. Correlates errors across systems and identifies root causes.
skill.summary: Analyze logs, stack traces, and error patterns to build evidence-based root cause hypotheses.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Production errors often hide across logs, stack traces, and recent changes. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structure evidence and prioritize likely causes.
actual_capabilities: Extracts error patterns from logs with regex-oriented guidance.
Reviews stack traces across languages to identify likely failure points.
Correlates errors with time windows, deployments, and service changes.
Builds timelines of error occurrences and rate changes.
Suggests monitoring queries for Elasticsearch, Splunk, and similar tools.
Produces root cause hypotheses with supporting evidence.
limitations: Requires relevant logs, stack traces, or incident context from the user.
Does not replace environment-specific validation or production testing.
Cannot access live systems unless the host AI tool provides that access.
May need clarification when permissions or success criteria are unclear.

use_cases.title: Triage Production Incidents
use_cases.description: Analyze recent errors, correlate them with deployments, and identify likely service failures.

use_cases.title: Debug Application Failures
use_cases.description: Review stack traces and logs to find code locations that likely caused the error.

use_cases.title: Improve Monitoring Coverage
use_cases.description: Turn recurring error patterns into detection queries and prevention checks.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Error Logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these error logs. Identify repeated patterns, affected services, and the most likely starting point.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Stack Trace
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this stack trace and explain the likely failure path. List the code locations that need inspection first.

prompt_templates.title: Correlate an Incident Timeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these logs, deployment notes, and timestamps. Build a timeline and identify changes that align with the error spike.

prompt_templates.title: Design Recurrence Detection
prompt_templates.prompt: Create monitoring queries and alert criteria for this error pattern. Include signals, thresholds, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A payment service started returning timeout errors after a deployment.
output_examples.output: The skill would group timeout messages, compare deployment timing, and highlight likely dependency or configuration changes.

output_examples.input: A stack trace points to several nested service calls.
output_examples.output: The skill would describe the failure path, identify the first meaningful application frame, and suggest files to inspect.

output_examples.input: A team needs alerts for a recurring database connection error.
output_examples.output: The skill would propose log search terms, alert thresholds, and verification steps for recurrence detection.

best_practices: Provide timestamps, deployment history, and representative log samples.
Separate confirmed evidence from hypotheses during investigation.
Validate proposed causes against system metrics and recent changes.
anti_patterns: Using one stack trace as proof without checking related logs.
Ignoring time windows, deployments, and service dependencies.
Treating generated hypotheses as production facts without validation.

faq.question: What inputs work best with this skill?
faq.answer: Logs, stack traces, timestamps, service names, recent changes, and monitoring output produce the best results.

faq.question: Can it search live production systems?
faq.answer: Only if the host AI tool has approved access to those systems. Otherwise, provide copied logs or exported data.

faq.question: Does it support Splunk or Elasticsearch?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill can suggest query structures and detection ideas for log aggregation tools.

faq.question: Can it find the exact root cause?
faq.answer: It can propose evidence-based hypotheses. Teams should validate them with tests, metrics, and system knowledge.

faq.question: Is it useful before an incident is resolved?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize symptoms, prioritize checks, and define immediate verification steps.

faq.question: How should teams use the output?
faq.answer: Use it as an investigation plan, then confirm each claim with logs, metrics, code review, or testing.
